title: Prime & Beyond is now open and turning heads with tender wagyu steak - NewsBreak
text:
By Brittany Misencik ,
19 hours ago
Prime & Beyond Wagyu Steakhouse is now open to the public at 650 E. Nine Mile Road.
Chef (and owner) Wayan Sumadi planned to open the doors to the glamorous new Pensacola restaurant slowly, but customers have been pouring in since last week’s soft opening to get their first taste of Sumadi’s famed, tender wagyu steak.
Services will start with just dinner but will grow to offer a lunch menu of the same quality at a lower price over time as the restaurant gets into its groove.
Prime & Beyond’s current hours of operation are listed online as 4 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. on Sunday through Thursday and from 4 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.
What is Prime & Beyond Wagyu Steakhouse in Pensacola? Prime & Beyond Wagyu Steakhouse brings a more modern, upscale dining option to the fast-growing East Nine Mile area. It's centered on marbled, incredibly tender wagyu beef, while keeping prices attainable for the Pensacola area, even though the beef is often considered a luxury item.
While Sumadi’s career has largely been spent in Asian cuisine—he recently sold his popular Sake Café Japanese restaurant—switching to a steakhouse specializing in wagyu brings an element of excitement and wow factor to the Pensacola area, he said.
What does Prime & Beyond look like? The physical design of the restaurant matches the elegance of the menu, which Sumadi had built from the ground up, to create an airy atmosphere with plenty of windows, wood-paneled, noise-cancelling ceilings, elegant chandeliers, dark teal booths and more.
The restaurant offers a variety of indoor and outdoor seating.
What’s on the menu at Prime & Beyond? The Prime & Beyond menu was crafted with intention by Sumadi, and executive chef Ross Johnson will help execute Sumadi’s vision.
The menu stars the famed Akaushi wagyu beef from HeartBrand beef in Texas, which has the largest herd of Akaushi cattle outside Japan.
Customers can take their pick of cuts, whether they want an 8-ounce center-cut filet mignon broiled to perfection, a highly marbled 7-ounce shoulder steak, or a 14-ounce New York Strip. While the quality of meat can have the cut stand alone in flavor, they can dress it up if they desire with house butters and sauces to take the flavorful cut to the next level, with enhancers such as a black garlic-bone marrow compound butter from the Black Garlic Market or a smoked aged blue cheese and house pork belly butter torched tableside.
Sumadi’s cut of choice, however, has to be a 14-ounce ribeye when it comes to wagyu.
If steak isn’t your thing, you’ll still be able to find your perfect menu fit through options such as the chef’s catch plate, crispy skin quail, rack of lamb with bourbon cherry glaze, or 12-ounce bone-in Duroc pork chop.
The menu will be filled with fresh produce, which will shine in dishes such as the farmers' market salad. Nothing sits in the kitchen for long, Sumadi said, and when they’re out of something for the night, they’re out.
The appetizer portion is full of can’t-miss menu items like the “Hot Stone” Japanese wagyu plate, house-cured pork belly sliders, and their house octopus carpaccio, with thin-sliced poached octopus drizzled with mango citrus vinaigrette.
Does Prime & Beyond serve alcohol? In addition to their showstopping steak selection, they’ll also have a walk-in wine case with a wide variety of wines by the glass or by the bottle, including some valued at up to $1,000 per bottle.
They will also have specialty cocktails at the bar, along with all the favorites, as well as sake and Japanese whisky. Some of their specialty cocktails include a spicy lychee, a tobacco-smoked old-fashioned, a hibiscus Hemingway daiquiri, and a special line of Prime martinis in addition to offering all the classics.
